objective: join a fresh Nigerian public-health prompt with two concise skincare safety myths without diagnosing, naming a product or making a treatment claim

sourcePost.timestampSource: live X time plus status chronology
sourcePost.observedText:
Tell me two dangerous lies some people believe.

I will go first:

1. That sunscreen causes cancer and should be replaced with natural oils.

2. That drinking Borax will detoxify the body and cure arthritis.

actionTimeAudit.method: fresh signed-in inspection of the exact public X thread immediately before submission

copy.post:
1. “If it burns, it’s working.”
2. “Natural means harmless.”

Skincare has suffered in the hands of both lies 😭

actionTimeConfirmation.confirmedUnit: the exact First Doctor target and previously shown text-only reply; no media, like, repost, quote-post, follow, direct message, schedule, spend or cross-post
actionTimeConfirmation.timing: the user instructed publication immediately before the action-time recheck

mechanism: Two familiar absolute-sounding skincare myths are answered in the same numbered rhythm as the source prompt, then tied together with one human reaction line.
careBoundary: General myth-warning language only. The reply does not diagnose an individual, assess a reaction or tell anyone to continue or stop a treatment.
claimBoundary: The reply rejects burning as an efficacy test and naturalness as a safety guarantee. It makes no product, ingredient, brand, treatment, price, stock or outcome claim.
